newsitem.title: USA: FTC delays decision on Staples, Office Depot merger.
newsitem.headline: FTC delays decision on Staples, Office Depot merger.

text.p: The federal government will delay until February its decision on whether to permit Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. to merge in a $3.3 billion deal, a Staples spokesman said Wednesday.

The companies had expected a decision this month, but the Staples spokesman said the Federal Trade Commission has now made a "second request" for additional information. While not unusual, such a request -- a formal procedure under federal law -- builds in some delay.
The spokesman said the government has now pledged to reach a decision in February. He was optimistic the FTC would approve the merger.
In a press release Monday, Staples announced simultaneous special stockholder meetings to approve the merger on Feb 27.

"Such meetings have been scheduled prior to receiving approval from the Federal Trade Commission in order to allow an expedited closing of the transaction upon FTC approval," the company said in a statement. "The FTC has not informed the companies of any decision regarding the proposed merger."
The two companies announced their proposed merger on Sept. 4, 1996. Staples plans to purchse Office Depot for $3.3 billion.
The companies argue that the combined power of the two office supply companies would permit them to pass on savings to customers.
Staples stock was off 12.5 cents at $20 on Nasdaq and Office Depot was unchanged at $20 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
